data.name: Abbaad
data.gender_notes: Abbaad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘abd, meaning servant. Abbaad is a name signifying a father of many children. The name Abbaad carries the meaning “Father of many” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abbaad usually hope their child will grow to embody father of many and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of a righteous and God-fearing father.
data.etymology: Abbaad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of many.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abbaad total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_english.name: Abbaad
in_english.long_meaning: The name Abbaad originates from the Arabic root 'abd', meaning servant or worshipper. It signifies a person who is devoted to the service of Allah. In Islamic tradition, names like Abbaad are chosen to reflect a family's aspirations for their child's spiritual growth and commitment to faith. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing humility and devotion. The name Abbaad is also associated with personality traits such as piety, obedience, and compassion.

As a name that signifies a father of many children, it is often seen as a desired name for families, particularly as a name for sons, as having many children is seen as a blessing from Allah and a sign of Allah's favor upon a family.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Abbaad also holds great spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of our duty as servants of Allah. Just as Abbaad signifies a father of many children, we are all 'abd (servants) of Allah, living our lives in submission to Him and striving to fulfill His commands and expectations. The name is a constant reminder of our role as His servants and the importance of staying devoted to Him in all aspects of our lives.
